newsitem.title: USA: VideoLabs to take $1.7 mln Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: VideoLabs to take $1.7 mln Q4 charge.

text.p: VideoLabs Inc said on Friday it would take a one-time restructuring charge of about $1.7 million in the fourth quarter.

The charge, most of which will be non-cash, will not effect the liquidity of the company. But it will reduce shareholder equity and may result in the company being in default on its current line of credit after a year-end audit to be completed in early 1997, the company said.

The charge will reflect changes in the valuation of the inventory purchased in anticipation of a new product line that was not successfully completed and has become technologically obsolete, the company said.
The charge will also cover retirement and severance payments to about 20 percent of the current employee base of the company; future warranty costs; and litigation reserves.
Company officials were not available for further comment.

"Rapidly changing technology and failure to fully meet the new product needs of customers has resulted in this one-time charge to earnings," chief executive officer James Hansen said in a news release.
Shares of VideoLabs fell 1/16 to 3/4 in Nasdaq trading on Friday.
